comment: Name orderings that compareNames (naturalOrder.ts) and compare_names (natural_order.rs) must both produce. Some file listings sort in the frontend and some arrive sorted from the backend, so a name has to land in the same place either way. Change one comparator and the other's fixture test fails. `input` is the order the names are given in, `expect` the order they sort into.

cases.name: a number too large for u64 still orders by value
padding orders before the number it pads
letters compare without regard to case
case alone is a stable tie-break, not a tie
an underscore orders after the digits it sits beside
a prefix precedes the name it prefixes
a digit orders before a letter in the same place
the real names of one champion's animation directory
a run of nothing but zeros is the number zero
